b.request: Inner join Laboratory to Patient on ID, exclude patients with NULL or blank SEX, compute each patient's mean ALB and mean UN/T-BIL ratio (excluding missing values and non-computable ratios), compute each sex's mean of those patient-level ALB values and mean of those patient-level UN/T-BIL ratios, calculate the overall mean of the sex-level ALB averages, filter to sexes where sex-level ALB average exceeds this overall mean, and display sex, its mean ALB, its mean UN/T-BIL ratio, and the amount by which its mean ALB exceeds the overall mean.
b.sql:
WITH patient_stats AS (
  SELECT
    p.ID,
    p.SEX,
    AVG(l.ALB) as patient_mean_ALB,
    AVG(CASE WHEN l.UN IS NOT NULL AND l.`T-BIL` IS NOT NULL AND l.`T-BIL` > 0 THEN l.UN / l.`T-BIL` END) as patient_mean_ratio
  FROM Laboratory l
  INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID
  WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND p.SEX != ''
  GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
sex_stats AS (
  SELECT
    SEX,
    AVG(patient_mean_ALB) as sex_mean_ALB,
    AVG(patient_mean_ratio) as sex_mean_ratio
  FROM patient_stats
  GROUP BY SEX
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(sex_mean_ALB) as overall_mean_ALB
  FROM sex_stats
)
SELECT
  s.SEX,
  s.sex_mean_ALB,
  s.sex_mean_ratio,
  s.sex_mean_ALB - o.overall_mean_ALB as excess
FROM sex_stats s
CROSS JOIN overall_mean o
WHERE s.sex_mean_ALB > o.overall_mean_ALB;

a.request: Linking lab records to patients by `ID` (dropping unmatched lab records), first average each patient's (`ID`, `SEX`) `ALB` and their per-test ratio of `UN` to `T-BIL`. Then, for each sex (leaving out patients whose `SEX` is blank or missing), average those patient-level figures. Which sexes have an average `ALB` above the mean of the sex-level `ALB` averages? Show the sex, its average `ALB`, its average `UN`/`T-BIL` ratio, and how far its `ALB` average is above that mean. Averages ignore missing values (including ratios that can't be computed); don't round.
a.sql: WITH lab_with_patients AS (SELECT l.ID, p.SEX, l.ALB, CASE WHEN l.`T-BIL` IS NOT NULL AND l.`T-BIL` != 0 THEN l.UN / l.`T-BIL` ELSE NULL END AS UN_T_BIL_RATIO FROM Laboratory l INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND p.SEX != ''), patient_averages AS (SELECT ID, SEX, AVG(ALB) AS avg_ALB, AVG(UN_T_BIL_RATIO) AS avg_UN_T_BIL_RATIO FROM lab_with_patients GROUP BY ID, SEX), sex_averages AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_ALB) AS sex_avg_ALB, AVG(avg_UN_T_BIL_RATIO) AS sex_avg_UN_T_BIL_RATIO FROM patient_averages GROUP BY SEX), overall_mean AS (SELECT AVG(sex_avg_ALB) AS mean_ALB FROM sex_averages) SELECT sa.SEX, sa.sex_avg_ALB, sa.sex_avg_UN_T_BIL_RATIO, sa.sex_avg_ALB - om.mean_ALB AS above_mean FROM sex_averages sa CROSS JOIN overall_mean om WHERE sa.sex_avg_ALB > om.mean_ALB

c.request: Linking lab records to patients by `ID` (dropping unmatched lab records), first average each patient's (`ID`, `SEX`) `ALB` and their per-test ratio of `UN` to `T-BIL`. Then average those patient-level figures for each sex. Which sexes have an average `ALB` above the mean of the sex-level `ALB` averages? Show the sex, its average `ALB`, its average `UN`/`T-BIL` ratio, and how far its `ALB` average is above that mean. Averages ignore missing values (including ratios that can't be computed); don't round. A blank sex means unknown, so those patients are dropped before grouping and before the mean is computed.
c.sql:
WITH lab_patients AS (
  SELECT 
    l.ID,
    p.SEX,
    l.ALB,
    CASE WHEN l.UN IS NOT NULL AND l.`T-BIL` IS NOT NULL AND l.`T-BIL` != 0 
         THEN l.UN / l.`T-BIL` 
         ELSE NULL 
    END as ratio_un_tbil
  FROM Laboratory l
  INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID
  WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND p.SEX != ''
),
patient_level AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    SEX,
    AVG(ALB) as avg_alb,
    AVG(ratio_un_tbil) as avg_ratio
  FROM lab_patients
  GROUP BY ID, SEX
),
sex_level AS (
  SELECT 
    SEX,
    AVG(avg_alb) as sex_avg_alb,
    AVG(avg_ratio) as sex_avg_ratio
  FROM patient_level
  GROUP BY SEX
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(sex_avg_alb) as mean_alb
  FROM sex_level
)
SELECT 
  sl.SEX,
  sl.sex_avg_alb as avg_alb,
  sl.sex_avg_ratio as avg_un_tbil_ratio,
  sl.sex_avg_alb - om.mean_alb as alb_above_mean
FROM sex_level sl
CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
WHERE sl.sex_avg_alb > om.mean_alb
ORDER BY sl.SEX

d.request: Join Laboratory to Patient on ID keeping only matched records, exclude patients with NULL or blank SEX before grouping, for each patient compute average ALB and average UN/T-BIL ratio (ignoring missing values and uncomputable ratios), then for each sex compute averages of these patient-level figures, compute the overall mean across all sex-level ALB averages, and report sexes whose sex-level ALB average exceeds this overall mean with their sex, sex-level ALB average, sex-level UN/T-BIL ratio average, and amount above the overall mean.
d.sql:
WITH patient_level AS (
    SELECT 
        p.ID, 
        p.SEX, 
        AVG(l.ALB) as patient_avg_alb,
        AVG(CASE 
            WHEN l.UN IS NOT NULL AND l.`T-BIL` IS NOT NULL AND l.`T-BIL` > 0 
            THEN l.UN / l.`T-BIL` 
            END) as patient_avg_un_tbil_ratio
    FROM Laboratory l
    JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID
    WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND p.SEX != ''
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
sex_level AS (
    SELECT 
        SEX,
        AVG(patient_avg_alb) as sex_avg_alb,
        AVG(patient_avg_un_tbil_ratio) as sex_avg_un_tbil_ratio
    FROM patient_level
    GROUP BY SEX
),
overall_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(sex_avg_alb) as overall_mean_alb
    FROM sex_level
)
SELECT 
    s.SEX,
    s.sex_avg_alb,
    s.sex_avg_un_tbil_ratio,
    s.sex_avg_alb - o.overall_mean_alb as amount_above_mean
FROM sex_level s
CROSS JOIN overall_mean o
WHERE s.sex_avg_alb > o.overall_mean_alb
ORDER BY s.SEX
